correctness.rationale: The standalone finite enumeration explicitly generates all 72 graph automorphisms and every subgroup by closure from generator prefixes (112 total, 26 conjugacy classes). It constructs 69/216/144 barycentric cells and all quotient cell-orbits, checks every vertex link is a circle or interval and every edge is incident to one/two triangles, and obtains each surface from exact Euler/boundary/orientability data. All seven type counts are asserted and reproduced in the included checker and 112-row certificate. Connectedness and compactness are inherited from the finite connected original cubical surface. The classification of compact connected surfaces gives the asserted homeomorphisms.

originality.rationale: The published unquotiented K3,3 unordered two-particle surface classification (Crisp–Wiest, 2004, Fig. 1) is expressly excluded as prior knowledge. The new statement classifies ordinary surface quotients for every one of 112 subgroups of the full 72-element graph symmetry group. Literature and published-finding corpus comparisons do not give a uniform or stronger equivalent classification for this exact object/action. A superficially close 30-subgroup chessboard-torus result is for a different complex and symmetry group, not a dominating theorem. The evidence is best-knowledge novelty, not proof of absolute priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible articles could contain the same full-subgroup K3,3 orbit table.
Most comparison material outside the key primary full texts was available only as indexed abstracts/summaries; these are not comprehensive negative evidence.
The classification concerns underlying topological spaces, not orbifold isotropy or group action conjugacy.

value.rationale: Classifying all 112 subgroups (26 conjugacy classes) produces a complete natural orbit-surface atlas for the canonical 72-element symmetry action, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It exhibits seven surface homeomorphism types, including a once-punctured torus and Klein bottle, different closed nonorientable genera and a disk full quotient; nonconjugate order-three actions have sharply different quotient surfaces. This supplies concrete input for later isotropy and surface-cover analyses without requiring a paper-scale general theorem.
